title: Open order index with ownership transfer
name: Open order index

questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code manages the lifetime of Order objects? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
After remove(id) returns, who owns the Order and when is it destroyed?
choices: The index still owns it until its destructor runs, and the returned pointer is a non-owning view
The caller owns it through the returned unique_ptr, and it is destroyed when that pointer goes out of scope unless the caller moves it elsewhere
It is destroyed inside remove before returning, and the unique_ptr holds a dangling pointer
Ownership is shared between the caller and byCustomer_ until the next purge

questions.prompt: purgeOlderThan collects stale ids under the lock, releases it, then calls remove for each id. What is the consequence of another thread removing one of those ids in between?
choices: Undefined behaviour, because the id now refers to a deleted order
A deadlock, because remove locks mu_ again while purgeOlderThan still holds it
The orders are deleted twice, once by each thread
remove finds nothing for that id and returns nullptr, so it is not counted and nothing is freed twice

questions.prompt: Why does the destructor delete only the pointers in byId_ and ignore byCustomer_?
choices: byCustomer_ is a cache and is rebuilt when the object is next constructed
unordered_map destroys raw pointers it contains automatically
Deleting both maps would double free: byCustomer_ only holds second, non-owning references to the same orders
byCustomer_ is always empty after the last remove call
